Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Ind:8962
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Binod Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 6 th Of April, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 7431 of 2023
 Ramesh
 Versus
 Sanjay And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Manish Jain - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Manoj Jain, learned counsel for the respondent No.
 Order

This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant assailing the impugned award dated 3.8.2023 passed by Additional MACT, Sardarpur,
District Dhar (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 120/2021, whereby an amount of Rs.1,09,958/- along with interest has been awarded to the appellant in the accident which occurred on 14.3.2021 involving the offending vehicle motorcycle M.P. 11 MX 6485.
2.
Facts of the case are that the appellant was going on a motorcycle.

The offending vehicle bearing registration No.M.P. 11 M.X.6485 came from front driven rashly and negligently and hit by respondent No.1, the driver of the vehicle which was owned by respondent No.2 as a result of which the appellant received grievous injuries.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has sustained fracture in bio-lateral xygometric arch as mentioned in para 23 of the award.
The income of the appellant was considered at the rate of Rs.7000/- per month.

Hence it is submitted that the amount awarded by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8962 2 MA-7431-2023 learned claims tribunal is on lower side and prays for appropriate enhancement in the compensation.

4. Per contra , learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company has opposed the prayer and submits that just and proper compensation has been awarded by the learned claims tribunal and no interference is warranted in the impugned award.

5. Heard and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
Ramesh vs Sanjay on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183686907/
1 6.
It is not not in dispute that appellant has suffered fracture in bio-lateral xygometric arch and has undergone 7 to 8 days of hospitalization in Mittal Hospital, Dhar.

Hence, taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, the appellant is further entitled for further lump sum enhancement of Rs.85,000/- by way of compensation in addition to the amount already awarded by the learned claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry the same rate of interest as awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The other terms and conditions shall remain intact.
7. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
